How many bits does b need?

Both budgets use the same 2,666 numbered motif graphs. For each fragment, a is its original NPE node ID. The graph fixes the elements, internal bonds and default atom states. Its occurrence specifies attachment atoms, bond types, relative pairing ranks and any changes in stereochemistry, formal charge, isotope or radical electrons.

At 2,666 entries, b is the integer encoding of those instructions. At 5,000 entries, the dictionary also stores the 2,334 most frequent graph variants across all motifs. If motif a has D stored variants, values 0 through D − 1 select them by local frequency rank. Other occurrences use b = D + q, where q encodes their instructions.

Dataset and counting conventions for [a,b]

The NPE vocabulary was trained on 50,000 ChEMBL 35 molecules with 3,000 node entries, including 300 frequent ring systems. The comparison retained 45,402 molecules whose SAFE fragment atom sets exactly matched the original NPE partition. The fixed-graph experiment counts a variant by the original NPE ID and the encoded graph instructions, including atom-state exceptions.

One integer ID per fragment

Each ID selects a numbered NPE motif graph and rules for connecting it to the other fragments in the sequence. The decoder builds the bonds from those IDs and the shared dictionary.

What makes 9,463 the minimum in this experiment?

Starting with 13,991 entries, the first joint grouping of site and partner rules used 9,482 IDs. Exact regrouping saved 19 more. The verified lower bound of 9,463 applies with the original fragment order, the same rule choices, fixed non-connection fields and one new ID per old entry. All counts refer to this full cohort.

Input ID sequence

From motif IDs to shared connection templates

Each fragment carries a pair [a,t]. The motif ID a selects a numbered reference graph. The template ID t selects instructions for joining it to other fragments and applying any changes in stereochemistry or atom state.
